n: In the seventh year, Jehoiada the priest took courage and made a covenant with five army commanders to restore the rightful king.
These commanders secretly gathered Levites and family leaders from throughout Judah to Jerusalem.
In the temple, the assembly made a covenant with the young king. Jehoiada declared: the king’s son shall reign, as God promised regarding David’s descendants.

f.w: as the LORD hath said of the sons of David

n: Jehoiada’s plan used the Sabbath shift change: a third of the incoming priests and Levites would guard the doors.
Another third would be at the palace and another at the Foundation Gate, with the people gathered in the temple courts.

f.g: Probably a temple gate; 2 Kings 11:6 calls it the gate Sur.

n: Only priests and ministering Levites, who were consecrated, could enter the temple building; everyone else would guard outside. Even in a crisis, holy space was respected.

f.w: keep the watch of the LORD
f.g: Observe the Lord’s requirements; keep their assigned posts.

n: Armed Levites were to surround the king and kill anyone who forced their way into the temple, staying with him at all times.
Everyone followed Jehoiada’s orders. He kept both the incoming and outgoing shifts on duty, doubling the guard.

f.g: Did not release the divisions going off duty.

n: Jehoiada armed the commanders with King David’s own spears and shields kept in the temple — a fitting symbol for restoring David’s heir.
Armed guards formed a protective line across the temple court, around the altar and the king.
They brought out the seven-year-old prince, crowned him, gave him “the testimony” (a copy of God’s law), and anointed him. The people shouted, “Long live the king!”

f.g: Likely the covenant law, which the king was to keep and study.

n: Athaliah heard the noise of people running and cheering, and came into the temple.
She saw the boy king standing by his pillar at the entrance, surrounded by officers, trumpeters, and rejoicing crowds. She tore her clothes and screamed “Treason!” — though she was the real usurper.

f.g: The king’s customary place by a temple pillar.

n: Jehoiada ordered the commanders to take her out between the ranks of soldiers and kill anyone who followed her — but not to kill her in the Lord’s house.

f.w: Have her forth of the ranges
f.g: Bring her out between the rows of guards.

n: They seized her and executed her at the Horse Gate entrance to the palace.
Jehoiada renewed the covenant: he, the people, and the king pledged to be the Lord’s people. Renewing covenants restores identity.

f.w: that they should be the LORD's people

n: The people tore down Baal’s temple, smashed its altars and images, and killed Mattan, Baal’s priest. Athaliah’s imported religion was removed.

f.g: A temple for Baal built in Jerusalem, probably under Athaliah.

n: Jehoiada restored temple service under the priests and Levites as David had organized it, with burnt offerings according to Moses’ law and joyful singing as David ordained.

f.w: as it is written in the law of Moses
as it was ordained by David

n: He stationed gatekeepers so no one ritually unclean could enter the temple — protecting its holiness.

f.w: that none which was unclean in any thing should enter in

n: With leaders and people, Jehoiada escorted the king from the temple through the Upper Gate into the palace and seated him on the throne.

f.g: The upper gate, connecting the temple and palace areas.

n: The people rejoiced and the city was at peace after Athaliah’s death. David’s line was restored.
